learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how the environment has become a massive political issue, the race for global resources, and the fight to protect our shared planet!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Environmental issues are political because they involve deciding who is responsible for the damage, who pays to fix it, and how natural resources are shared among nations.
Areas that belong to no single country and must be managed jointly by the international community. Examples include the Earth's atmosphere, Antarctica, the ocean floor, and outer space.

The principle that all countries are responsible for protecting the environment, but developed countries (who polluted more during industrialization) must bear a heavier burden than developing countries.

The global struggle and political maneuvering for control over vital resources, primarily oil and water. 'Who gets what, when, where, and how' often dictates international relations and even causes wars.
The struggle of indigenous communities worldwide who are losing their lands, forests, and traditional way of life due to government and corporate exploitation of natural resources.

fun_activity.title: 💧 The Water War Scenario
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine two countries share a single major river. The upstream country wants to build a dam for electricity, which will reduce water for the downstream country's farmers. Write a 3-point diplomatic treaty to solve this 'Resource Geopolitics' conflict fairly!

exam_tips: 📌 CBDR (Common but Differentiated Responsibilities) is one of the most tested topics. Know the definition and why developing nations support it.
📌 Mention the 1992 Earth Summit (Rio Summit) as the turning point where environment became a central global political issue.
📌 Give examples of the Global Commons: Antarctica, Outer Space, and the Ocean Floor.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set binding targets for industrialized countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
⭐ Global North (developed) focuses on current ecological conservation, while Global South (developing) focuses on economic development alongside conservation.
⭐ The survival of indigenous populations is fundamentally tied to the protection of their local environments.
